01.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, Marei bar Mar, Rav Huna and his son Rabba
01.event: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda sent Marei bar Mar to ask Rav Huna whether the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar on bills of divorce.
01.turn: Before the question reached him, Rav Huna died.
01.outcome: Rav Huna's son Rabba answered instead, reporting his father's tradition that the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar.
01.summary: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda sent a question through Marei bar Mar to Rav Huna: does the law follow Rabbi Elazar on divorce documents? Rav Huna died before the question arrived. His son Rabba answered in his place, saying his father had taught that the law does follow Rabbi Elazar, and that other scholars said the same in Rav's name.

02.actor: a maidservant of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household
02.event: The maidservant immersed herself in a ritual bath.
02.turn: When she came up, a bone was found between her teeth.
02.outcome: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi required her to immerse again.
02.summary: A maidservant in Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household immersed in a ritual bath. After she came out, a bone was found stuck between her teeth. Rabbi ruled that the immersion did not count and she had to immerse again.

03.event: Rav Yehuda, nearly blind, struggled hard to read documents himself before signing them.
03.turn: Ulla told him it was unnecessary, since Rabbi Elazar and Rav Nahman had documents read to them by court scribes and then signed.
03.summary: In his old age Rav Yehuda could barely see, yet he strained to read every document before signing it. Ulla told him he need not, because great authorities like Rabbi Elazar and Rav Nahman had scribes read documents aloud to them and then signed. The text does not say whether Rav Yehuda changed his practice; it moves on to a legal qualification.
03.missing: Whether Rav Yehuda accepted Ulla's advice.

07.actor: Bonyam ben Nunyam and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
07.event: A wealthy man, Bonyam ben Nunyam, sent Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi a gift of extremely fine linens.
07.summary: A wealthy man named Bonyam ben Nunyam sent Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi a gift of four kinds of fine linen. The fabrics were so thin they could be folded to the size of a nut or a pistachio, yet opened out large enough to clothe him. The passage then uses this to define a word.
07.missing: Any turn or outcome; the gift is described but nothing follows from it.

08.event: Colleagues challenged Ben Azzai for preaching the duty to have children while never marrying.
08.outcome: Ben Azzai answered that his soul yearned for Torah and the world could be sustained by others.
08.summary: Ben Azzai taught that failing to have children is like shedding blood. His colleagues pointed out that he preached this well but did not practice it, since he had never married. He replied that his soul longed only for Torah, and others could keep the world populated.

09.actor: a man who came before Rabban Gamliel
09.event: A man told Rabban Gamliel that on his wedding night he found no sign of virginity.
09.turn: Rabban Gamliel suggested the man had approached at an angle, explaining with a parable about a door that opens only if pushed aside.
09.summary: A man came to Rabban Gamliel claiming that his new wife showed no sign of virginity. Rabban Gamliel suggested the man may have entered at an angle and so met no obstruction, comparing it to someone in the dark who finds a door open only because he pushed the bolt aside. The text does not say how the case was decided.

11.actor: Rava and Rav Mari bar Rahel
11.event: Rava declared Rav Mari bar Rahel, son of a gentile father and Jewish mother, fit to marry into Israel and appointed him an official of Babylonia.
11.summary: Rav Mari bar Rahel had a gentile father and a Jewish mother. Rava ruled that he was of acceptable lineage and even appointed him to an official post in Babylonia. The passage then justifies the appointment despite the rule that officials must come from among one's brethren.
11.missing: Any turn or consequence; the passage is an event followed by legal justification.

12.event: Rabbi Yohanan spent eighteen days with Rabbi Oshaya and his twelve students.
12.summary: Rabbi Yohanan recalled spending eighteen days with Rabbi Oshaya, learning only one point about the Mishna's spelling from him. He also remembered that the study hall was so crowded that four students sat in each square cubit. The rest of the passage reconciles his conflicting statements.
12.missing: A turn or ending; these are reminiscences rather than a story.

13.event: While Ameimar sat in judgment a man removed a feather from his head; a man covered spittle lying before Mar Ukva.
13.turn: In each case the helper turned out to have a lawsuit to bring before the judge.
13.outcome: Each judge declared himself disqualified from hearing that man's case.
13.summary: A feather landed on Ameimar's head while he was judging, and a man came over and removed it. Ameimar asked what brought him, and the man said he had a case; Ameimar declared himself disqualified because of the favor. In a similar episode a man covered some spittle in front of Mar Ukva, turned out to have a case, and Mar Ukva likewise refused to judge it.

14.event: Rabbi Zakkai recited a baraita before Rabbi Yohanan on the status of the area between side posts.
14.outcome: He told Rabbi Zakkai to go teach it outside, i.e., not in the study hall.
14.summary: Rabbi Zakkai recited a teaching before Rabbi Yohanan that the area under a cross beam has a restricted legal status. Rabbi Yohanan dismissed it, telling him to go and teach it outside, meaning it did not belong in the study hall.

15.event: While sitting before Rav Ashi, Ravina saw a man tying his donkey to a palm tree on Shabbat and shouted at him.
15.turn: The man ignored him, so Ravina pronounced him excommunicated in his teacher's presence, then worried this was disrespectful.
15.outcome: Rav Ashi reassured him that where God's name is desecrated, no deference is owed to a teacher.
15.summary: Ravina was sitting with his teacher Rav Ashi when he saw a man tying his donkey to a palm tree on Shabbat, which the Sages forbade. Ravina shouted at him, but the man paid no attention, so Ravina declared him excommunicated. Afterwards Ravina asked Rav Ashi whether acting like that in his presence was disrespectful. Rav Ashi told him that when God's name is being desecrated, honor for a teacher does not apply.

16.actor: Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
16.event: Rabbi Abbahu reported in Rabbi Yohanan's name that the halakha follows Rabbi Yohanan ben Beroka.
16.turn: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi silently turned their faces away in disagreement.
16.summary: Rabbi Abbahu sat and taught, in Rabbi Yohanan's name, that the law follows Rabbi Yohanan ben Beroka. Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, sitting opposite him, turned their faces away to show they disagreed, without contradicting him aloud. The Gemara then debates who the speaker was and why they stayed silent.

17.event: Rabbi Yosei met Elijah the prophet and asked how a woman is a helper to a man.
17.outcome: Elijah answered that she turns raw wheat and flax into bread and clothing, lighting up his eyes and standing him on his feet.
17.summary: Rabbi Yosei met Elijah the prophet and asked him what the verse means by calling a wife a helper. Elijah answered that a man brings home wheat and flax, but he cannot chew raw wheat or wear raw flax; his wife turns them into bread and clothes. In that way she brightens his eyes and puts him on his feet.

18.event: On his deathbed Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi made prophetic pronouncements about places in Babylonia.
18.turn: He revealed that the people of Bireta DeSatya had that day trapped fish on Shabbat, been excommunicated by Rabbi Ahai and become apostates, and that Adda bar Ahava was being circumcised.
18.outcome: He announced that on that day Rav Yehuda was born in Babylonia.
18.summary: As Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi lay dying, he described places in Babylonia: one whose people were Ammonites, one full of mamzerim, one where two brothers swapped wives. He said that in Bireta DeSatya the people had that day caught fish on Shabbat from an overflowing ditch; Rabbi Ahai excommunicated them and they all abandoned Judaism. He said that in Akra DeAgma a boy, Adda bar Ahava, was that day sitting in Abraham's lap, newly circumcised, and that Rav Yehuda had just been born in Babylonia.

19.actor: Rabbi Yohanan (told by Rabba bar bar Hana)
19.event: Rabba bar bar Hana and others followed Rabbi Yohanan to eat the famous fruits of Genosar.
19.turn: Rabbi Yohanan ate a vast quantity, more than a three-se'a basket could hold.
19.outcome: He then swore he had not yet tasted anything nourishing.
19.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana recalled going with Rabbi Yohanan to eat the sweet fruits of Genosar. The group would take ten fruits each when they were a hundred people, or a hundred each when they were ten, and each hundred fruits overflowed a large basket. Rabbi Yohanan ate them all and then swore that he had not yet eaten anything that nourished him.

20.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and his sons
20.event: On his deathbed Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi called in his sons one at a time.
20.turn: He gave his younger son Rabbi Shimon the orders of wisdom, and his older son Rabban Gamliel the procedures of the office of Nasi.
20.outcome: He instructed Rabban Gamliel to lead with firmness and cast fear on his students.
20.summary: As he was dying, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi asked for his younger son, Rabbi Shimon, and passed on to him the principles of wisdom. Then he asked for his older son, Rabban Gamliel, and handed him the procedures of the patriarchate, telling him to rule with authority and keep his students in awe. The deathbed scene began earlier and his death is not shown here.
20.missing: The start of the deathbed narrative and its ending (Rabbi's death) lie outside the segments shown.
